title: Sorting
intro: The attributes of your emails: what you want to know of each one, to organise yourselves — where it stands, how urgent it is, who takes care of it, what it is about. Each says how it is decided when an email is sorted. Boards filter on them.
formIntro: An attribute has a few values. When an email is fetched, a rule can give it one; members can always set it by hand.
name: Name
valuesHint: Type a value and press Enter. Click its dot to choose its colour. A “member” attribute takes the members of the organisation.
fixed: The name and the values of a pre-configured attribute are fixed: the application relies on them.
ruleIntro: Written in Elo, a small expression language: it costs nothing to run and says exactly what it does. It is given the email as _ and answers a value, or null to say nothing.
tryHint: Trying a rule changes nothing: it shows what the rule would say of your twenty most recent emails.
confirmDelete: Delete the attribute “{name}”? Boards stop filtering on it.
sortAgain: Save and apply to the emails already kept
confirmSortAgain: Save “{name}” and apply its rule to every email already kept? Values set by hand are left as they are.
sortedAgain: {examined, plural, one {# email} other {# emails}} looked at, {changed, plural, =0 {none changed} one {# changed} other {# changed}}.
sortAgainHint: A rule applies to the emails fetched from now on. To have it look again at those already kept, apply it to them: values set by hand stay, emails replied or placed by a member stay where they are.
skill: Download the skill for an AI agent
skillHint: Rather have an AI assistant write the rule? Give it this skill: it says what a rule is given, what it must answer, and enough of Elo to write one — for this attribute and its values. Paste what it writes above, and try it.
noteAi: Decided by the AI when sorting
noteUser: Set by hand: sorting leaves it as it is
noteByHand: A value you choose here stays as you put it.
stepRuleText: Runs when the email is fetched. It costs nothing, and says exactly what it does.
stepAiText: Only where you ask for it, and only for emails the rule said nothing of.
stepHandText: Any member who sees the email can set a value. It then stays as they put it.
hintElo: Costs nothing, when the email is fetched.
hintAi: Uses AI tokens, when the organisation has the AI sort.
hintEloAi: The AI only where the rule says nothing.
hintNotYet: Not yet for an attribute you made: the AI decides only the two pre-configured ones.
hintAiSorting: One request per 20 emails fetched; the AI is sent their sender, subject, beginning of text and attachment names.
